messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ratecard v2026.2 patch is scheduled tonight. One of our healthtech POCs asked for a temporary 50% discount on the 'POC-SKU' and wants commit crediting clarified. Who should I loop in for approvals? :wave:

maria: @alex loop Deal Desk and Finance. We need a documented exception and start/end dates. Also call out whether this affects grandfathering for existing commits.

ryan: FYI, the POC lead insists on a commit credit if they convert within 90 days. Is that standard? :thinking:

tanvi: Not standard. We normally map POC usage to trial credits, not commit credits. If they want commit crediting we need a formal exception and a sign-off from Revenue Ops + Legal.

alex: Ok — can Deal Desk confirm process? Drafting a short ask now.

deal-desk-bot: @alex Please include: customer name, POC SKU, requested discount %, POC start/end, expected conversion window, and whether they ask for commit backdating. See https://redwood.internal/docs/deal-desk/exception-form

alex: Drafted the ask:

```
Customer: HelixCare
SKU: POC-SKU-HEALTH
Discount: 50% for 60 days
Conversion window: 90 days
Requested commit credit: Yes, backdate to POC start if converted
Reason: Regulated data onboarding requires longer validation
```

maria: Adding Legal and Revenue Ops will slow but that's the right path. @ryan can you confirm expected ARR if converted (for revenue impact)?

ryan: Estimated ARR = $120k annualized if converted. Will update with a clear breakdown by next morning.

finance-bot: Auto-note: Any commit-crediting exception requires finance review for revenue recognition impact. Please attach P&L impact statement.

tanvi: Also note quantization: If approved, specify whether discount is one-off or recurring for first invoice. That affects billing ledger tagging.

alex: Perfect — I'm routing this now to Deal Desk. Will ping again when I have Ryan's numbers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
